description: Luftwaffe performance data for priority German aircraft (Bf 109 E/G-2, Fw 190 A-8/D-9) drawn from Kurfürst, wwiiaircraftperformance.org, and Rechlin/Messerschmitt transcriptions. All numbers graded.
sources_main: kurfurst.org (Messerschmitt Datenblatt May 1942, Rechlin Kennblatt 1943, Erla averages)

bf109_g1_g2.configuration: Steig- und Kampfleistung (1.3 ata / 2600 rpm), clean fighter
bf109_g1_g2.notes: Messerschmitt AG Datenblatt May 1942. Rechlin G-1 trial: 650 km/h at 6400 m (fixed tailwheel, ~12 km/h penalty). Soviet NII VVS G-2: 666 km/h at 7000 m. Erla average of 13 production aircraft: 652 km/h at ~6700 m.

bf109_e.source: British RAE/AFDU captured trials + Messerschmitt V15a protocol
bf109_e.level_speed_notes: V15a (prototype E-1): ~493 km/h corrected at SL, 572 km/h at 4800 m. Captured trials confirm competitive low-medium altitude performance.
bf109_e.notes: Flaps and undercarriage up. CLmax ~1.4 flaps up.

fw190_a5_a8.notes: Multiple Focke-Wulf sheets (Oct 1943–Oct 1944). A-5 typical ~567 km/h SL / 656 km/h at 6.3 km. A-8 sheets show 557–578 km/h SL and ~644–652 km/h at rated altitude. Cooling flaps and armament affect numbers.

fw190_d9.source: Focke-Wulf flight reports and Rechlin trials (wwiiaircraftperformance.org)
fw190_d9.level_speed_notes: With MW50 / Sondernotleistung: up to ~606 km/h SL and higher at altitude. Dry figures lower. Early reports note drag from ETC and wheel covers.
fw190_d9.notes: Data thinner than A-series. Primary reports exist but full matched-mass tables less consistently transcribed.

gaps: Full altitude-by-altitude power and cooling state for every point still incomplete
Stall CAS/EAS at matched mass for G-2 and 190 still missing
D-9 dry vs MW50 separation needs more precise primary tables
